clue.text: Not easy to take in answer from this record

indicators.note: to take in means the first word for 'hard' swallows the second piece

parts.note: something not easy is hard

explanation.surface: A difficult document from which to absorb any reply.
explanation.walkthrough: HANSARD is the official printed record of debates in the UK Parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: Hansard is the verbatim transcript of British parliamentary proceedings, a published register of what was said.

clue.text: Victor is married — shows fortitude

parts.note: a victor is a winner, a hero

explanation.surface: A winner who has wed displays courage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shows' is a link word between the wordplay and the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Heroism is great courage and bravery, which is what fortitude describes.

clue.text: Emigrant uses his head perhaps in this dream of retirement

indicators.note: perhaps signals that emigrant plus a letter might be arranged another way
the head of his is its first letter

explanation.surface: A homesick expatriate thinks hard about a bad dream of leaving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges EMIGRANT plus H (the head of 'his'). 'Retirement' means going to bed, not leaving work.
explanation.definitionFit: A terrifying dream comes after retiring for the night, hence a dream of retirement.

clue.text: Thespian performance by soldiers

parts.note: an act is a performance on stage
OR stands for other ranks, soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: A dramatic show put on by troops.
explanation.definitionFit: A thespian is a stage performer, a player in drama.

clue.text: Boxer's neckwear

parts.note: a boxer is a breed of hound, and what it wears round its neck is also a cleric's stiff white band

explanation.surface: What a prizefighter wears round the neck.
explanation.walkthrough: The boxer here is a breed of dog, not a fighter.
explanation.definitionFit: A dog wears a band round its neck; the same name is given to a clergyman's stiff white band.

clue.text: Dormouse, for example, or mole

explanation.surface: A naturalist lists hibernating creatures alongside the burrowing mole.
explanation.definitionFit: A dormouse hibernates, lying dormant all winter; a mole is a spy planted to lie inactive for years until activated.

clue.text: Flying midwife?

parts.note: folklore says babies are delivered by a big white bird, making it an airborne deliverer of infants

explanation.surface: A nurse who delivers babies by air.
explanation.definitionFit: Nursery folklore has this large wading bird deliver newborns to parents.

clue.text: Retaining one's vigour — always on the go?

parts.note: ever means always
a green light means go

explanation.surface: Staying energetic by being constantly busy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the' links the two pieces; 'go' is the signal shown by a green traffic light.
explanation.definitionFit: Evergreen describes someone perennially fresh and lively, like a plant that never loses its leaves.

clue.text: Resentment at its height vocally

indicators.note: vocally means the word is spoken and heard rather than read

parts.note: a peak is a height or summit

explanation.surface: Bitterness at its highest point, expressed out loud.
explanation.definitionFit: Pique is a feeling of irritation or wounded pride.

clue.text: What to do after on-off performance?

definitions.text: What to do after on-off performance?

parts.words: What to do after on-off performance?
parts.note: an actor who has gone on and then off stage must come back on again

explanation.surface: A question about what to do after an erratic show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on-off' suggests something intermittent, but here it is an actor who has gone on and then exited.
explanation.definitionFit: Coming back on stage after an exit is the next move in a play.

clue.text: Tories' privilege

explanation.surface: A complaint about the entitlements enjoyed by the Conservative party.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tories form the political wing called by this name; a privilege is an entitlement one holds.

clue.text: Go and request dancing together -fantastic outcome

indicators.note: dancing together means these letters jig about and combine into a new order

explanation.surface: Going off and asking someone to dance leads to a bizarre result.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dancing together' shuffles the letters of GO and REQUEST; 'outcome' merely links.
explanation.definitionFit: Grotesque means bizarre or wildly distorted, as something fantastic in the old sense of fanciful.

clue.text: Engage to put in the earth and seal

parts.note: to inter is to bury a body in the ground
to lock is to fasten or seal shut

explanation.surface: A proposal to bury something and close it up tight.
explanation.definitionFit: Gears that engage mesh together, fitting into each other.

clue.text: Welcome cry

explanation.surface: A shout of welcome.
explanation.walkthrough: In Scots, to greet means to weep or cry.
explanation.definitionFit: To welcome someone is to hail them; in Scottish dialect the same word means to weep.

clue.text: Funds for the channel

explanation.surface: Money set aside for a television station.
explanation.definitionFit: Funds are money resources; a channel is a medium or method through which something is done.

clue.text: Walked on water by the sound of it

definitions.text: Walked on water by the sound of it

parts.words: Walked on water by the sound of it
parts.note: walking through wet mud or water makes a sucking, slurping noise

explanation.surface: A miracle of walking on water, judged by the noise it made.
explanation.definitionFit: To squelch is to tread through soggy ground with a wet sucking noise.

clue.text: A square of cheese

explanation.surface: A block of cheddar cut square.
explanation.walkthrough: Leicester Square is a well-known square in central London; Red Leicester is an English cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: Leicester Square is a famous London plaza, and the same name labels a hard orange English cheese.

clue.text: Making an impression by giving an order

explanation.surface: Impressing people by issuing commands.
explanation.definitionFit: To indent is to press a dent into a surface, and also to place an official requisition for goods.

clue.text: Dog food on the back of a lorry

parts.note: to dog someone is to follow or tail them
board means meals, as in bed and board

explanation.surface: Pet food stacked on a truck's rear.
explanation.walkthrough: A lorry is a British truck; 'on' just links the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A tailboard is the hinged rear flap of a truck or cart.

clue.text: Finnish flag we hear is so variegated

definitions.text: Finnish flag we hear is so

explanation.surface: A remark that the flag of Finland looks multicoloured.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Finnish' sounds like 'finish', and the flag waved at the finish of a motor race is the chequered flag.
explanation.definitionFit: A chequered pattern is a mixed pattern of squares of differing colour, so variegated in look.

clue.text: State the whole counthry's in, according to O'Casey

definitions.text: State the whole counthry's in, according to O'Casey

parts.words: State the whole counthry's in, according to O'Casey
parts.note: Sean O'Casey's Juno and the Paycock ends with the line that the whole world is in a terrible state of disorder

explanation.surface: A playwright's verdict on the condition of Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: Captain Boyle in O'Casey's Juno and the Paycock says the whole world is in 'a terrible state o' chassis', his mispronunciation of chaos.
explanation.definitionFit: O'Casey's character uses this word as a dialect version of chaos, a state of disorder.

clue.text: No sound made by Rosinante?

parts.note: the word no said as nay chimes with the noise a horse makes, and Rosinante is Don Quixote's horse

explanation.surface: A question about silence from Don Quixote's old horse.
explanation.walkthrough: Rosinante is the nag ridden by Don Quixote; a 'no sound' is 'nay', which is exactly the noise a horse makes.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse's cry, heard as the old word for no, is the noise Rosinante would make.

clue.text: SHAPE one up on U.S Dept. of Defense

indicators.note: one up on means the number in the name is raised by one, from five to six

parts.note: the US Department of Defense is housed in and known as the Pentagon

explanation.surface: A geometric figure one better than the American military headquarters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one up on' changes the Greek prefix for five, PENT-, to the one for six, HEX-.
explanation.definitionFit: A six-sided polygon is a geometric figure.

clue.text: Capri landscape showing sign of Spring

indicators.note: showing means the letters are on display within the words Capri landscape

explanation.surface: A view of the Italian island revealing the first signs of the season.
explanation.definitionFit: This month falls in spring and is one of its signal months.

clue.text: He wrote about a Dutch entanglement initially

parts.note: re means about or concerning

indicators.note: initially means the opening letters of Dutch and entanglement are taken

explanation.surface: An author composed a piece on a Dutch love affair.
explanation.walkthrough: Charles Reade was a Victorian novelist, author of The Cloister and the Hearth.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Reade was a nineteenth-century English novelist and dramatist.

clue.text: Small bed with a light behind it

definitions.text: Small bed with a light behind it

parts.words: Small bed with a light behind it
parts.note: a small bed for flowers sits on a sill with a glazed pane, a light, behind it

explanation.surface: A child's cot placed in front of a lamp.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'light' in old usage is a pane of glass; the 'small bed' is a flower bed, not a cot.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a planter fixed to a sill: a tiny flower bed with the glazing behind it.

clue.text: Vital element in decisive battle

parts.note: a life-giving classical element forms the opening of the name of Wellington's decisive 1815 victory

explanation.surface: The key factor that won a crucial fight.
explanation.walkthrough: Waterloo, Wellington's decisive defeat of Napoleon, begins with this element.
explanation.definitionFit: It is one of the four classical elements and is vital for all life.

clue.text: Sad missing start of card game

indicators.note: missing start of means the opening letter of the word for sad is lost

parts.note: sombre means sad or gloomy

explanation.surface: A gloomy player without the first card of the game.
explanation.definitionFit: Ombre is a seventeenth-century trick-taking game played with forty playing cards.

clue.text: Eight pats cooked in a dish

indicators.note: cooked suggests the letters of eight pats are prepared and mixed up

explanation.surface: A recipe in which eight pats of butter go into a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: This long thin pasta is served as an Italian meal.

clue.text: Depend on second-rate hemp

parts.note: B is a grade below A, so second-rate
to hang on something is to depend on it

explanation.surface: Relying on inferior cannabis.
explanation.definitionFit: Bhang is an Indian preparation of cannabis, the plant otherwise called Indian hemp.

clue.text: Second uncle named in the Merry Wives

parts.note: uncle is old slang for a pawnbroker, a moneylender

explanation.surface: A relative mentioned in Shakespeare's comedy who is the second uncle.
explanation.walkthrough: Uncle is old slang for a pawnbroker. The Merry Wives of Windsor is Shakespeare's comedy, whose cast includes the foolish suitor Abraham Slender.
explanation.definitionFit: Abraham Slender is a character in Shakespeare's comedy The Merry Wives of Windsor.

clue.text: Urged on perhaps to get the poet's reward

indicators.note: perhaps hints that urged on is a possible arrangement of other letters

explanation.surface: Encouraged in the hope of winning the bard's prize.
explanation.definitionFit: Guerdon is an archaic, poetic word for a recompense or prize.
